clue.text: One entering school tests works fine

indicators.note: the numeral for one goes into the school tests, sitting within them

parts.note: SATS are the national tests taken in English schools
I is the Roman numeral for one
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A newcomer joining the school's exam programme is getting on nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: SATS are standard assessment tests sat by pupils in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that is fine is acceptable or adequate, good enough to pass.

clue.text: Turn to gas to get high

definitions.meaning: to pass from solid straight to vapour, a chemistry verb

explanation.surface: Someone inhaling fumes to get a buzz.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry verb for a solid vaporising directly, and an adjective for something exalted or elevated in spirit.

clue.text: XXXX perhaps, and Aussie finally is tight

parts.note: XXXX is four Roman tens, an example of tens

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word Aussie

explanation.surface: An Australian has had too much of a famous lager brand and is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: XXXX is a Queensland beer, which makes 'tight' (drunk) look like the sense; the X's are really Roman tens.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tight and taut both describe something stretched with no slack, as nerves or muscles.

clue.text: Flimsy blouse held up in public eye

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a blouse is one of a woman's tops
light, insubstantial

explanation.surface: A sheer blouse hoisted on display for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be in the public eye is to be under media attention, the full glare of publicity.

clue.text: Monotonous back-up covering Queen

indicators.note: the support word wraps over the royal letter, holding it within

parts.note: back-up is help or support, aid
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Dull support singers backing a monarch, or a rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: dry and dull, lacking interest or variety.

clue.text: Menace subsequently trapping rebel without cause initially

indicators.note: the word for afterwards holds the shortened rebel inside it

parts.note: then, afterwards

indicators.note: without signals that a letter is dropped from the rebel word

parts.note: to react against authority is to rebel

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word cause

explanation.surface: A James Dean figure, the rebel without a cause, menaces people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like part of the film title Rebel Without a Cause, but it signals dropping the first letter of 'cause'; 'trapping' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to menace someone is to intimidate them with warnings of harm.

clue.text: Rise of an Emperor Haile Selassie follower

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, interchangeable with a
a tsar is a Russian emperor

explanation.surface: The ascent of an emperor, Ethiopia's Haile Selassie, and his devotees.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: Rastafarians revere Haile Selassie, the Ethiopian emperor, as divine, so a devotee follows him.

clue.text: Smart if I celebrate taking trick

indicators.note: taking means the letters are lifted from within the phrase Smart if I celebrate

explanation.surface: A clever person rejoicing after winning a trick at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ruse or clever deception, cunning stratagem.

clue.text: Moved up, straddling horse announced as punch perhaps

indicators.note: the turned departure word sits astride the horse letters, around them
in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: gone, as in moved away

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, its sound giving two letters

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse, said as G G

explanation.surface: A rider moving up astride a horse is said to throw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the departure word in this down clue; 'announced' means the childish gee-gee is heard as two letters, which 'straddling' puts inside. 'Punch' is the drink, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: eggnog is one kind of punch, a mixed drink served in a bowl.

clue.text: Belt holder securing many rounds?

parts.note: describes a shoulder belt with loops that carries lots of cartridges

explanation.surface: Something like a belt or holster that keeps many rounds safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a soldier's shoulder belt fitted with loops for carrying ammunition cartridges.

clue.text: Kid's programme entertaining child

explanation.surface: A children's television show amusing a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: a sprog is a small child, a youngster.

clue.text: Fancies holding large models

indicators.note: the word for notions holds the size letter inside it

parts.note: fancies are notions or ideas
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone who fancies big fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: perfect examples or paragons, standards to aspire to.

clue.text: Britain and America opposing heretical German

parts.note: V for versus, against

explanation.surface: Two Allied nations ranged against a dissenting German.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Bavarian comes from Bavaria, a state in southern Germany, so is one kind of German.

clue.text: Quarantine perhaps, for instance with spots returning

indicators.note: returning means the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: acne is spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Isolation advised, say, when a rash of spots comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: to quarantine an animal is to shut it in a cage or pen, as kennels do.

clue.text: Following check, expose piece, one on board

parts.note: CH is the chess notation for check

explanation.definitionFit: Description: the head of a company's board of directors is one who sits on it, presiding.

clue.text: Cuddling young bird

definitions.meaning: a chick still in the nest

explanation.surface: A picture of a fledgling snuggled into its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Participle for snuggling close against someone, and a noun for a chick too small to leave its nest.

clue.text: The French composer first in twitter ends 'Gypsy'

clue.text: Young man's gripping extravagant upturned rump

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A youth seizing an over-the-top raised backside.

clue.text: A container in this way produces plant

parts.note: a can is a container
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A recipe for producing a plant: take a pot and do it like so.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: acanthus is a Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, copied on Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Foreigners like to eat right

clue.text: Bowled over by view from pavilion

clue.text: Clearly too tense inside

parts.note: overly means too, excessively

clue.text: Pervert's in hot water

clue.text: Stabled by Poseidon, Augeas turned over dung!

clue.text: Regret catching computer key for 'Save'

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
